source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: The current safe fetch-listener adapter rejects payloads longer than i32::MAX, creates an nsIStringInputStream, converts bytes to nsCString and uses SetByteStringData so the stream owns a copy. A stream that borrows a temporary Rust buffer can outlive that buffer and leave an invalid pointer. SAFETY comments explain the size and ownership conditions at each unsafe call. Manual Rust boundary proposal: justify both value validity and lifetime in the unsafe-call comment; a live local byte vector is not proof that an asynchronous consumer can borrow it. This current adapter retains the length limit from the original implementation; no large-message allocation or runtime lifetime test was performed.
title: Rust-to-XPCOM message streams must own copied data beyond the Rust buffer
